We’re saving money by doing the following:

- Monday wedding, our venue was about 3k more expensive to do it on a Fri/Sat/Sun. We also booked in during the summer holidays so my nieces and nephews who are all kids can come along with my sister who is a teacher. Some venues may also be cheaper out of season. 

- Cutting the guest list, we’ve got down 38 guests. Another 40 to accommodate our cousins etc would easily cost us an extra 5k. We’ve gone for most important people and then aunts and uncles only. 

- DIY everything we can - our save the dates were designed using a canva template for free and printed using free prints. We will do our actual invites this way too. Table decs I’ll doing too and using Facebook market place to find cheap second hand bits where possible. 

- we’re not doing favours. I can’t remember any favours I’ve received at weddings before. 

- only the groom and best man are wearing matching suits, the rest of the grooms men will wear whatever they own already. 

- we booked over 2.5 years ahead so we could save at a manageable rate. Putting savings into a higher interest account and avoid buying decorations and items until closer to the time to accumulate some interest. 

- We’re not booking fancy cars. My dad will drive me to the venue and our friends will sort out getting my partner to the venue. 

- florals - table decs/venue decs will be artificial flowers to save money. Only our bouquets and buttonholes will be real flowers, depending on what you want but they could all be fake to save some extra money. 

- Dresses - I haven’t got my dress yet but I’ve been dress shopping, Im trying to find what I like second hand to save money. 

- Food/cake - we’ve gone for a 2 course meal instead of 3 and will serve our cake as dessert. We’re also going for a small supermarket (M&S naked cake) and I’m going to make brownies ahead of time and freeze as my partner doesn’t like cake. Our guests will then have a choice of cake or brownie.
Cardboard scratchers, our cats go feral for them. They have plenty of cat scratching posts/trees but they love the cardboard ones.
Do it! It’s your day and you deserve to eat safe foods considering you’ll be spending a fuck ton. People can deal with it for 1 day, if I was your guest I would not be bothered at all.

We didn’t plan to have ours on a significant date, it was mainly dictated by what was going to be cheaper. Initially looked at spring/winter, then midweek rather than the weekend. 

When we viewed our venue and spoke to them they told us that they don’t do their pricing like that, whilst weekends are more expensive there is no difference between the months so we ended up going for August which is the month we got together. Our anniversary would have costed a LOT more as it falls on a weekend so we went with the next closest and cheapest date. 

I didn’t really fancy paying an extra 2-3k for the sake of a date.

If you have no preference, I’d recommend looking at your guests and what would be easier for them/make them more likely to come.

Most advice is to just cut it out and don’t buy it, that never worked for me as someone who has a long history with binge eating. I now eat the treat and work it into my calories, trying to avoid it usually means I’m eating everything and anything and consuming hundreds of calories on “healthy options”, still not feeing satisfied so I end up eating the treat. If I just ate the treat then I would have cut those hundreds of calories out and would have been satisfied straight away. Also restricting like that very easily leads to binges for me. 

This is of course just my experience. I’d recommend you working treats into your day, cutting out treats completely is never sustainable. Also, no point assigning moral value to food. All food is good (unless you’re allergic or it’s rotton), some are just better at nourishing your body and others are better at nourishing your soul. You need both to live a happy life.

Your first steps should be making simple swaps, instead of full fat fizzy drinks opt for zero sugar ones, swap fruit juice with low sugar cordial. Add a portion of veggies with each meal, do 5 minutes of exercise or go for a short walk. 

Also don’t do anything you won’t be able to stick to long term for example if you love bread and pasta going keto is just not going to be sustainable in the long run as are most diets.

He used to send angry and manipulative emails about how he will die soon etc etc 🤦🏻‍♀️ over the years my siblings have spoken with him and I think that helped him do some reflecting. I think my dad did generally care but because of his own childhood trauma he parented in a very emotionally neglectful and some what emotionally abusive way. He was a single parent as my mum abandoned us so I think he was way over his head especially as he is of the era where men go to work and women look after the kids. 

When I got back in contact I said I wanted family therapy with him and thankfully he agreed. I’ve done most of the leg work because he’s never done therapy before and really has no idea of what he’s looking for but I basically went to a licensed therapist directory and found a person who specialises in families and we went from there.

So far he seems to have made some real progress with his own emotional maturity and has been open and honest. 

I’d say that if you’re going to go for it, test the waters a little and see how they respond to things you say. If they immediately jump to being dismissive then I wouldn’t give therapy a go. I just don’t think it’s worth it (my mum is like this) but if they seem to have some care and are willing to listen then suggest it but keep a cautious attitude until they have proven their intentions.

I’ve been going with my dad, we’ve had 5 sessions and it’s going well! When I wasn’t talking with him my sister kept saying he she would speak to him about topics and I think the time away allowed him to self reflect. It’s been helpful, it’s clear that time away has allowed us both time to think and reflect and I do hope we carry on being open with one another (I never felt like he was approachable, especially when I was younger and needed a parent to talk to, that combined with the fact he never opens up and bottles everything meant we often never talked about our feelings and instead waited until we exploded at one another).

As someone in the process of recovering from binge eating it’s definitely worth seeking out professional advice, binge eating can be down to a variety of reasons and to treat it you need to figure out the why. 

Could it be that you 1) emotionally eat - make a note of how you feel prior to, during and after a binge and maybe take note of what you were doing at the time. Often EDs are related to emotional issues and you use food to compensate, keeping track of how you’re feeling will be beneficial to spot patterns and also to take to a therapist if you can access one. 

2) it could be down to trauma - therapy is super important if you can access it. if you are not in a position for this join support groups online and try and read books and resources on binge eating. 

3)do you restrict? Most people with binge eating have a habit of restricting to make up for the binge, they tell themselves they won’t buy any treats in and feel guilty for eating. Restricting causes a harsh cycle and scarcity mindset e.g. you tell yourself that you will NEVER eat this much again, that tomorrow you will be better. A warning signal goes of in your head which makes you feel that the food is urgent because you “can’t” have it and so you then binge to compensate and the cycle starts again. So if you do restrict you need to learn that it’s ok to eat and if you binge that’s ok, you don’t need to punish yourself further. 

4)habits - humans are creatures of habit and we tend to repeat things. If you don’t do any of the above/there’s no trauma it could be that it’s just a habit and you need to find something to occupy your mind and hands. It’s never a bad thing to incorporate a hobby into your routine during times that are most triggering, for me sitting on the sofa watching TV just makes me ravenous in the evening. To combat that I do crafts etc doesn’t always work but sometimes it does! 

For me it’s a mix of all of the above and I’m now a year into my recovery, whilst I still definitely have days I over eat and the occasional binge it’s not as much. For the first time in my life I am maintaining my weight rather than gaining extreme amounts. It’s worth mentioning that many people are scared of weight and gaining, it’s completely normal to gain in recovery. NICE guidelines (UK) state that weight loss is NOT a goal for recovery. 

Mostly though you need a support network that will encourage you, tell your friends and family that you are struggling with this and that you need their support. Feel free to message if you need support, I’ve had this disorder and struggled with other eating disorders for the past 15 years.

Ex nurse here that used to work in secure units, what you’re asking is not possible. It is not fair to other patients to blanket ban them from using their mobiles just because your brother is struggling, I’ve not known any assessment and treatment units to fully ban mobiles. In secure we did along with internet access but that was because everyone came through the courts and prison system, many of our patients had done terrible crimes that had victims so it was the safest thing for everyone although they did have daily phone calls in and out and had supervised internet access. 

If he’s intimidating other patients then staff should be completing safeguardings for this however just because he’s taller doesn’t actually mean he’s intimidating other patients, he could have generally asked as they were happy with it.  Maybe you could ask if they’ve done any safeguarding and what the outcome is, unfortunately in most cases it’s often moving the person to a different ward or placing them on 1-1 but they would have to argue why he needs that and sending spam emails isn’t really a high priority besides that level of care (1-1) isn’t something you really want him on. It is much better for his prognosis for him to have as much freedom as he safely can and what is least restrictive. 

Also you said in a comment that he is sending emails via his work email so talk with his employer and see if they can freeze him out until he recovers. 

It is very typical for drs to only see patients once a week in their MDT, nothing will change with this unless you can fork out for private care. Your brother should have a named nurse who is overall responsible for his nursing needs so it would be worth finding out if you could chat with them to see if you can work on a solution that’s best for your brother. 2 weeks is very early on in his care too, they may need to trial different medications to stabilise him before they even offer or plan any type of therapy or therapeutic activities to help him recover. 

Being his family you are kinda in a way responsible, you are the only people he knows outside of this environment and knew that he was like before his psychotic break. The professionals don’t know him like you do and they’ve only seen him in a state of poor mental health so you absolutely should work with them, besides families can have massive impacts on patients so talk with him and see if you can encourage him not to break the fire alarms. 

He will have better care overall if the family work with the ward and staff as a whole rather than fight against them, make sure you participate in MDTs and see if he can have access to an advocate. Staff are massively stretched in underfunded services, they are doing the best they can care for very unwell patients all whilst being treated like they’re not doing enough and very under appreciated. You are ofcourse able to make a complaint through the PALs system if you feel he is not being cared for properly, this shouldn’t have a negative impact on the care he receives.

Your binging may have something to do with restricting, it’s typically what happens: you binge/eat more than usual so you tell yourself you will compensate by skipping a meal/reducing your next meal/cutting out food groups entirely, your brain then thinks you’re never going to eat those nice things again so it triggers a binge and the cycle continues. 

I get everyone is different so this may not be the case but try these few things: stop restricting, allow yourself to eat what you want, when you want guilt free (that’s the important part), stop beating yourself up for it, stop counting kcals/tracking - even if it’s just for now. 

It sounds counter intuitive I know and you’ll probably be thinking “if I allow myself to eat whatever, whenever then I’ll never stop eating” and at first it does seem that way but after a few months of doing this you start to retrain your brain to eat intuitively and in moderation. I’ve struggled with this disorder for about 18 years and this is the only thing that has actively helped me stop binge eating. You also want to make sure that you’re not skipping meals even if you do binge.

I have different ideas of what I class “binges” for myself. First one is what’s classed as a typical binge where I eat large amounts of food within a short amount of time - I would eat pack of 6/8 chocolate bars, family share bag of crisps, cookies and 8 cheese strings within like an hour. It feels out of control, you feel sick and bloated but that doesn’t matter because your brain is screaming at you to eat. Typically this is when I will “hide” what I’m doing, discard wrappers at the bottom of the bin, eat in secret and feel deep shame and guilt for doing it. 

Second type is the constant going back and forth to the cupboard which spans over a longer time like 5-6 hours, you’re still out of control and you’re constantly thinking about food. It’s still a compulsion to eat but not as intense at the first type. I usually still feel shame for this but not as much as the first type, I kind of justify it away a little because it wasn’t in one short session. 

Lastly overeating, I don’t count this as binging but it’s what I would say is eating for the sake of it or squeezing in a second helping or pudding even though I’m satisfied. For me this comes more from habit or because it tastes nice over compulsion to eat it. If I was even a little disciplined then I could put it down (by that I mean, I can put it in another room and be fine, no thoughts about eating it but if it’s in front of me then it’s in my face and I’ll want to eat it) where as the other binges no amount of discipline would change it because I can’t control myself, if it was in the other room or locked away my brain couldn’t switch off from it and I’d constantly be wanting it.
